data.title: Evercore Raises Apple Stock (AAPL) Price Target to $380. Here's Why

data.title: Deutsche Bank Unit DWS Shutters US Real Estate Fund While Xtrackers ETFs Drive Strong Inflows
data.description:
Deutsche Bank (DB) asset manager (DE:DWS) plans to sell off all assets inside its U.S. real estate investment trust following investor withdrawals. RREEF Property Trust (ZRPTAX) held a net asset value of $203 million at the end of June. Chief Executive Officer Todd Henderson stated that the fund faced persistent challenges bringing in fresh cash alongside a long stretch of high redemption requests.

The plan to wind down the trust requires stockholder approval before liquidation can start. The board of directors and executive management team at RREEF Property Trust plan to host a special shareholder meeting to vote on the asset sale. Once approved, the board intends to pay out net cash proceeds from property sales to stockholders over time.

Interest Rate Hikes Have Made U.S. Real Estate Less Appealing to Buyers

RREEF Property Trust was an early model of a net-asset value REIT, which allowed individual investors to buy and redeem shares based on underlying property values. The trust bought property staples like retail stores and shipping warehouses across the U.S. market. Similar non-traded vehicles raised billions from everyday investors, but DWS struggled to build hype for its fund.

Data from investment bank Robert A. Stanger Co. shows that the DWS trust saw net cash leave the fund in 14 out of the past 15 quarters. In all fairness, liquidating the fund and giving capital back to investors is the right move given the lack of buyer traction.

DWS' Broader ETF Business Is Thriving

While private real estate vehicles face large cash withdrawals, DWS's broader ETF business continues to pull in strong investor demand. The firm's flagship Xtrackers ETF division registered billions in net inflows across global markets. This brought total Xtrackers assets under management past €330 billion. Everyday investors and institutions are choosing publicly traded funds for low fees and simple stock market access.

data.title: Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Slips Despite New Win as the "Safest Cheap EV in America"
data.description:
While many look to electric vehicle giant Tesla (TSLA) for a lot more than just electric vehicles these days—like robots, artificial intelligence (AI), and energy storage—Tesla still makes electric cars. And these cars won a surprising new accolade, with the Model Y declared "…the safest cheap EV in America." This did little to enthuse investors, though, and Tesla shares dropped modestly in Friday afternoon's trading. Tesla stock has seen a 14.05% loss in its share price over the past year.

The Surprise Winner in Cheap, Safe EV

Electric vehicles are expensive, when compared to gas-powered cars. And a lot of car shoppers find even gas-powered cars too expensive these days. But a new report from Climate Crisis 247 notes that the best deal among EVs is the Model Y. The report noted that the Model Y offers the best crash protection of an EV with a price tag of under $40,000.

The news comes at an excellent time for Tesla, as its share of the EV market in the United States is back over 50% after two years of ongoing losses. This gives Tesla two important advantages that it can put into its marketing: being a significant value provider, and being able to provide that value without skimping on protective features that keep drivers safe.

More Megachargers

Tesla is also set to bring a set of new Megacharger sites to Forum Mobility electric-truck depots throughout California, a Reuters report noted. The new chargers are geared toward heavy vehicles, and will give users access to 30 megawatts of charging capacity.

Tesla will operate the Megachargers at FM Francis in Ontario, as well as FM Adeline and FM Coliseum in Oakland, the report noted. Tesla's Megachargers are catching on, as fleet operators have already offered commitments for over 330 Tesla Semi trucks for the site at Rancho Dominguez. That site will also open up for other commercial trucking operations to use, which will likely be welcome for any other electric truck operator.

data.title: Axon's (AXON) Dilution Fears Look Overstated
data.description:
Axon Enterprise's (AXON) ongoing dilution fears look overstated, in my view. The stock plunged on September 15 after the company announced a $1 billion convertible-note offering, adding another worry to its heavy stock-based compensation. However, the notes carry 0% interest, convert initially at $652.06 per share, and mature in 2031. Axon also bought protection against dilution up to $1,049.94.

Meanwhile, underlying growth continues to surge, with Q2 revenue rising 35% to $904 million, marking the tenth consecutive quarter of over 30% growth. Management's "operating system for public safety" is taking shape, and I think this financing provides useful capital without creating the immediate dilution investors feared. Thus, my AXON stock forecast remains bullish.

For context, Axon Enterprise is a cloud-based technology company that offers public safety solutions.

data.title: Nucor Stock Drops 5.8% as Disappointing Third Quarter Profit Forecast Hits Steelmakers
data.description:
Shares of Nucor (NUE) fell 5.8% on Friday to trade near $249.74 after the steel manufacturer issued a quarterly profit outlook that came in below Wall Street expectations. The drop made Nucor the single worst-performing stock in the S&P 500 for the session. Fellow steelmakers also took a hit, with Steel Dynamics (STLD) slipping 4.6% and Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) dropping 1.8%.

Nucor expects adjusted earnings between $5.55 and $5.65 a share for the third quarter, while Steel Dynamics guided for $5.34 to $5.38 a share. Both profit outlooks missed analyst estimates, causing a negative market reaction across the steel sector. Higher prices for steel raw materials continue to push input costs up for manufacturers.

Analysts Are Still Still Bullish on NUE Stock

Even with the initial market pullback, industry analysts view the conservative guidance as a short-term issue rather than a sign of structural weakness. Wells Fargo analyst Timna Tanners trimmed her price target on Nucor to $280 from $285 while keeping an Overweight rating on the stock. She noted that tight conditions in the steel sheet market remain a primary driver, though seasonal demand soft spots and rising imports could ease U.S. steel prices late in the year.

data.title: Markets at Midday: U.S. Stocks Fall as 10-Year Treasury Yield Moves Back Above 5%
data.description:
U.S. equity markets are sliding lower at midday on Sept. 18 as the yield on the 10-year Treasury rises back above 5%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite indices are each in the red to end the trading week as spiking bond yields continue to pressure stocks. The 10-year Treasury yield was at 5.002% at noon hour, having risen from 4.966% earlier in the day.

The yield on the 2-year Treasury note rose more than five basis points to 4.743%, while the 30-year Treasury yield is up four basis points to trade at 5.336%. Yields on government bonds have steadily risen during the week as prices for U.S. Treasurys weaken. One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.

A Losing Week for U.S. Equities

The benchmark S&P 500 index is headed for a losing week, even after the index rebounded strongly on Sept. 17 following the Federal Reserve raising interest rates by 25 basis points, its first hike in three years. At noon on Friday, the S&P 500 is down 0.25%, while the Dow is down 0.48%, and the technology-laden Nasdaq (NDAQ) is trending 0.15% lower.

data.title: SpaceX Stock Falls After First Orbital Starship Flight Is Delayed
data.description:
Space and satellite company SpaceX (SPCX) fell more than 2% at the time of writing after delaying Starship's first orbital flight by six days. Flight 14 is now scheduled for September 28 instead of September 22. The mission is an important test because Starship is expected to reach about 275 kilometers above Earth and complete roughly six orbits. SpaceX also plans to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites during the nearly 10-hour flight.

Each V3 satellite is designed to add about one terabit per second of capacity to Starlink. As a result, a successful mission would test whether the much larger rocket can start deploying the next generation of satellites that SpaceX needs to grow Starlink.

In addition, the Super Heavy booster is expected to attempt an offshore landing, while Starship will target a controlled splashdown in the Pacific. This means that SpaceX does not plan to attempt a "Mechazilla" tower catch on this flight.

Ron Baron Sees Huge Potential in Starlink

The delay comes as retail investors have already been taking money off the table. According to Barron's, JPMorgan (JPM) estimates that retail investors sold roughly $570 million of SpaceX shares over the past three weeks. About $250 million was sold in the latest week alone. However, billionaire investor Ron Baron remains extremely bullish.

Baron Capital owns about $25 billion of SpaceX shares, and Baron told CNBC that he estimates Starlink currently generates nearly $18 billion in annual revenue. He believes that figure could eventually reach $1 trillion within 10 years.

Baron also suggested that Starlink could generate $700 billion to $800 billion of EBITDA at that scale. In his view, those economics could support a valuation of roughly $14 trillion to $15 trillion, which are Baron's long-term estimates rather than company guidance.

He also addressed the speculation that SpaceX and EV maker Tesla (TSLA) could eventually combine. Baron said he would support whatever decision Elon Musk makes.
